raw_response:
I've farmed these same 6 mu for 50 years. Never went to school, can't read the writing on the fertilizer bags, but I know this soil better than any book. I'm 70 now, and my back aches when the weather turns. My son works construction in Handan, sends home some money every few months. Six people in the house, including two grandkids. We need the cotton for cash and the maize to feed the pig and for eating money.

I stopped doing that wheat-maize double crop years ago — too much rushing for an old man, and I can't handle harvesting wheat in the June heat then planting maize the same week. So this year, same as last year: 3 mu of cotton and 3 mu of spring maize. Split right down the middle.

**Cotton:** I'll plant around April 22, when the elm trees leaf out. That's my calendar. I buy the seed from the supply shop in town, the same kind my younger brother used last year, about 30 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I put down one big bag of that compound stuff for every mu and a half — two bags for the 3 mu. That's what I've always done. If the plants look yellow in July I might throw on a handful of urea, but probably not; fertilizer got expensive again this year. I'll water twice from the well: once after planting if the spring wind dries the soil out, and once when the white flowers open. The electricity for the pump costs too much to water more than that. I'll spray for worms four times — the bollworms and red spiders never miss a year. Picking is the hard part. My wife and I do most of it, but if the bolls open heavy, I'll hire two women from the village for 5 days at 100 yuan a day. Last year I got 260 kg of seed cotton per mu. This year I hope for 280, but you never know.

**Maize:** I'll plant around May 1, after the cotton is in the ground. Hybrid seed, about 25 yuan per mu. One big bag of compound fertilizer for every 2 mu — so one and a half bags for the 3 mu. That's it for fertilizer. Maybe throw some urea when the plants are knee-high if we get good rain, but I probably won't spend the money. Water twice if July and August are dry. One spray of herbicide when the maize is small to kill the weeds. My wife and I can handle all the maize work ourselves, no hired help. We should get 400 to 450 kg per mu if the summer storms don't flatten it.

All together — seeds, fertilizer, medicine for the plants, electricity for pumping water, and maybe some hired picking — I reckon about 2,100 yuan. My son sent money home last month, but my granddaughter needs things for school, and my wife's medicine isn't cheap. I can't pour everything into the field. Better to have some cash in the mattress than all of it tied up in the dirt.
